chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī and Abī Qatādah, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who comes upon water in a channel or a pond: may he perform ghusl from janabah with it, or perform wudu from it for salat, if he cannot find any other water, while the water does not amount to a saʿ for janabah nor a mudd for wudu, and it is scattered? So what should he do, while he fears that wild beasts may have drunk from it?
He said: If his hand is clean, then let him take a handful of water with one hand and sprinkle it behind him, and a handful in front of him, and a handful to his right, and a handful to his left.
If he fears that it will not suffice him, he should wash his head three times, then wipe his skin with his hand, for that will suffice him.
And if it is wudu, he should wash his face and wipe his hand over his forearms, his head, and his feet.
And if the water is scattered and he is able to gather it, then he should do so; otherwise, he should perform ghusl from this and from that.
So if it is in one place and it is a small amount that does not suffice him for his ghusl, there is no blame upon him if he performs ghusl and returns the water into it, for that will suffice him.

key_terms.السِّبَاعُ: wild beasts whose drinking from the water is feared
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer) for which ritual purity is required
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.غَسَلَ: he washed, referring to the required act of washing
key_terms.مَسَحَ: he wiped, referring to the act of wiping in purification
key_terms.يُجْزِيهِ: it suffices him, meaning it fulfills the requirement

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if only a small scattered amount of water is available for ghusl or wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on using a small and scattered amount of water for ghusl and wudu when no other water is available. It describes how one should use such water carefully and minimally, and states that this is sufficient in the circumstance. The narration is significant in discussions of ritual purity and the rulings of used water in Shia fiqh.
